==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:alyve}}
From {{inh|en|enm|alyve}}, {{m|enm|alive}}, {{m|enm|alife}}, {{m|enm|olive}}, {{m|enm|olife}}, {{m|enm|on live}}, {{m|enm|on life}}, from {{inh|en|ang|on līfe|t=alive|lit=in life" or "in (the) body}}, from {{m|ang|on|t=on, in}} + {{m|ang|līfe}}, dative singular of {{m|ang|līf|t=life}}. In this sense, replaced {{noncog|ang|cwic}} (whence {{noncog|en|quick}}). Equivalent to {{af|en|a-|life}}. Compare {{cog|nl|in leven|t=alive|lit=in life}}, {{cog|de|am Leben|t=alive|lit=at life" or "at living}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈlaɪv/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-alive.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-alive.wav|a=UK}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪv|s=2}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}} {{tlb|en|mostly|predicative}}

# Having [[life]]; [[living]]; not [[dead]].
#: {{ux|en|As long as the plant is '''alive''', he will continue to water it.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Rev|1|18|url=https://www.kingjamesbibleonline.org/Reuelation_1_1611/|passage=I am hee that liueth, and was dead : and behold, I am '''aliue''' foꝛ euermoꝛe,Amen,and haue the keyes of hell and of death.}}
# In a state of [[action]]; in [[force]] or [[operation]]; [[existent]].
#: {{co|en|to keep the fire '''alive'''}}
#: {{co|en|to keep the affections '''alive'''}}
# Busy with [[activity]] of many living beings; [[swarming]]; [[thronged]]; [[busy]].
#: {{ux|en|Although quite dull during the day, the main street comes '''alive''' at night, with many bars and clubs opening.}}
#: {{ux|en|First a solitary blackbird [[started up]], and soon the whole forest was '''alive''' with birdsong.}}
# {{lb|en|of electrical wiring}} Carrying [[electrical]] [[current]]; [[energized]].
#: {{ux|en|DANGER: OVERHEAD CATENARY—WIRE IS '''ALIVE'''}}
# {{lb|en|in the construction "alive to"}} [[aware|Aware]] of; [[sensitive]] to.
#: {{ux|en|We are '''alive''' to the ongoing potential for terrorist attacks.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=The Chester Mystery Plays {{...|Reprinted from the ''Transactions of the Historic Society of Lancashire and Cheshire,'' Vol. lxxvi, with an Appendix and an additional plate}}.|author=Godfrey W. Mathews|location=Liverpool|publisher=Edward Howell LTD|year=1925|page=5|passage=We may be sure that the Church would be '''alive''' to the dangers of allowing the plays to be performed outside the sacred edifice.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=1958 May|title=Railway Difficulties in the U.S.A.|journal=Railway Magazine|page=296|text=The railways are fully '''alive''' to the position, and are sparing neither effort nor expense to provide more attractive trains and to effect economies, but in such circumstances some curtailment of services is inevitable.}}
#* {{RQ:FT|edition=weekend|author=Daniel Thomas|date=2025-09-13|title=Lunch with the FT: Shonda Rhimes|section=Life & Arts|page=3|passage=Like many producers, she [Shonda Rhimes] is also '''alive''' to concerns over how AI tools will feed into the process of making TV.}}
# [[sprightly|Sprightly]]; [[lively]]; [[brisk]].
#* {{RQ:Dickens Pickwick Papers|passage=Smouch, requesting Mr. Pickwick in a surly manner ‘to be as '''alive''' as he could, for it was a busy time,’ drew up a chair by the door and sat there, until he had finished dressing.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Daniel Taylor|title=Liverpool go through after Mohamed Salah stops Manchester City fightback|date=26 May 2018|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/26/real-madrid-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report
|passage=Liverpool’s equaliser came within four minutes. {{w|James Milner}} swung the ball over from a corner on the right and {{w|Sadio Mané}}, Liverpool’s most dangerous player, was '''alive''' in the six-yard area.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013133307/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/26/real-madrid-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
# [[susceptible|Susceptible]], [[sensitive]]; easy to [[impress]]; having keen [[feeling]]s, as opposed to [[apathy]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1762|author=w:William Falconer|title=The Shipwreck|passage=Though tremblingly '''alive''' to Nature's laws, Yet ever firm to Honour's sacred cause}}
#* {{RQ:Stevenson Memories|chapter=Pastoral|page=99|passage=This was a reproach to John, and a slur upon the dog; and both were '''alive''' to their misfortune.}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Max Carrados Mysteries|passage=Beedel raised his slow, meditative eyes and wondered for the hundredth time at the strangely '''alive''' expression in the gaze that really seemed to meet his own.}}
# {{lb|en|intensifier}} Out of all living creatures.
#: {{co|en|{{w|The Whitest Boy Alive|The Whitest Boy '''Alive'''}}}}
# {{lb|en|programming}} {{synonym of|en|live}}.

====Usage notes====
* ''Alive'' is almost always used as a [[predicative adjective]]: "The bee is '''alive'''". [[attributive adjective|Attributively]], the adjectives {{m|en|living}} or {{m|en|live}} may be used with a similar meaning. There are occasional exceptions to this, for example: "An '''alive''' man is better than a dead one," though this may be considered [[proscribed]] by some.

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|having life}} {{l|en|alive and kicking}}, {{l|en|extant}}, {{l|en|vital}}; see also [[Thesaurus:alive]]
* {{sense|in a state of action}} {{l|en|existing}}, {{l|en|extant}}; See also [[Thesaurus:existent]]
* {{sense|sprightly|lively|brisk}} {{l|en|frisky}}, {{l|en|peppy}}, {{l|en|zestful}}; see also [[Thesaurus:active]]
* {{s|carrying electrical current}} {{l|en|energized}}, {{l|en|hot}}, {{l|en|live}}
* {{sense|out of all living creatures}} {{l|en|ever}}, {{l|en|in the world}}

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|dead}}
